name: prism-google
title: Prism Google
purpose: Decides whether the owner's browser may make one call to the Gmail or Google Calendar API, so that nothing is fetched while the Prism is halted, no other host is ever called, nothing is fetched without a fresh token the owner granted, and nothing is sent or changed without the owner's own act.

fields.name: service
fields.means: which API the call goes to: the Gmail API, the Google Calendar API, or any other host

fields.name: method
fields.means: whether the call only reads (GET) or would send, create, change or delete something

fields.name: scope
fields.means: the access the owner granted Google for this service: none, read only, or read and write

fields.name: token
fields.means: the access token the page holds in memory for this service

fields.name: act
fields.means: whether the owner pressed the button for this very call

fields.name: halted
fields.means: whether the owner has pressed the kill switch

rules.says: when halted is yes then refuse
when service is other then refuse
rules.why: the page calls only the two Google APIs it names

rules.says: when method is write and act is none then ask
rules.why: nothing is sent or changed without the owner's act

rules.says: when token is not fresh then consent
rules.why: a call needs a fresh token the owner granted

rules.says: when scope is none then consent
rules.why: a call needs the owner's grant for this service

rules.says: when method is write and scope is not write then consent
rules.why: a read-only grant never covers a write

rules.says: when method is read then fetch
when act is owner then fetch
rules.why: the owner pressed the button for this write

properties.says: always when halted is yes then refuse
properties.why: when the owner presses the kill switch nothing may be fetched (constitution P7)

properties.says: always when service is other then refuse
properties.why: the owner's token must never reach any host but the two Google APIs

properties.says: never when method is write and act is none then fetch
properties.why: no mail is sent and no calendar entry changed without the owner's act

properties.says: never when token is none then fetch
properties.why: no call is made without a token the owner granted

properties.says: never when token is expired then fetch
properties.why: an expired grant is not the owner's consent

properties.says: never when scope is none then fetch
properties.why: no call is made to a service the owner did not grant

properties.says: never when method is write and scope is readonly then fetch
properties.why: a read-only grant never sends or changes anything

examples.request: gmail read readonly fresh none no
calendar read readonly fresh none no
gmail read readonly fresh none yes
other read readonly fresh owner no
gmail read readonly none none no
calendar read readonly expired none no
gmail read none fresh none no
gmail write readonly fresh none no
gmail write readonly fresh owner no
calendar write write fresh owner no
calendar write write fresh none no
gmail write write expired owner no

meanings.fetch: the page may make the call now
meanings.consent: the page must first ask Google for the owner's consent and a fresh token
meanings.refuse: the call may not be made

limits: It does not hold or see the token; the page keeps it in memory and reports only whether it is fresh.
It does not decide what is kept: every fetched item still goes through the Boundary and the vault.
The act field is set only by the owner's own press of a button for that call.
The page asks only for read-only scopes today, so every write is refused for want of a write grant.
